I always found history to be boring until I grew to enjoy learning it as an adult. The way he taught Delaware history to my kids was so great. He used props, encouraged participation and engagement, and adapted his plan to make the experience enjoyable to my kids. It was neat for me to see the more reserved kids warm up to volunteering, and they enjoyed it. I learned a lot about local history personally. I'm so glad we got to experience history with Aaron and his family.Kind Sir, Thank you for your glowing review and your family's eagerness to volunteer! Gratefully yours, Aaron Bradford Written August 19, 2025This response is the subjective opinion of the management representative and not of Tripadvisor LLC.Review of: Liberty EncountersVisited August 2025Traveled with familyWritten August 17, 20251 of 5 bubblesNo workers, no customer serivice, ended up more $$$ than other airlines.This is by far the worst flight experience and customer service experience I have had in my 20 years of travel. Our original flight was delayed overnight by 20 hours in Atlanta- not cancelled. We were unable to change the booking on the website and essentially try to pay either small fee or the difference in the fair. There were 300 people in line to speak to their customer service, today there was 400. We are traveling with infant twins and breastmilk and therefore had to rebook on another flight the next morning because the long wait and 5AM departure time was untenable. No refunds, no ability to pay a difference in fare, no one to talk to, nothing. THEN once we paid for all of the luggage AGAIN.. they lost one of our bags. Our luggage with all the baby gear and mom clothes- no one at the airport was there to help me report the lost bag and the website (which I tried 15 times, and so did an airport worker who was trying her hardest to help me in the absence of the person who's job it was) was not submitting my form even though I was well within the 4 hours from touch down. I am currently on the phone waiting for HOURS to speak to a representative to try to find my lost bag. All this has cost more than two tickets with Delta or American- who provide available customer service, flight amendments when necessary, and sure as heck would have someone to find a lost bag. I filed a complaint with the DOT cause this was ridiculous.Review of: Avelo AirlinesVisited March 2026Traveled with familyWritten March 17, 2026Robin LAdams, Massachusetts227 contributions4 of 5 bubblesearly history of the area and court systemThis was the very original state house court house in Delaware. It was similar to the one in Dover. There is a guided tour which takes about 45 minutes. You can spend time in the exhibit upstairs that has a history of the area, from the Revolution up to today, and about the early Swede, English and Dutch settlers fighting like little kids over who owned what. You will learn that Delaware was originally part of Pennsylvania, because William Penn wanted to be able to easily access the river and ports. Well worth an hour visit. Free, donations accepted.Review of: New Castle Court HouseVisited July 2025Traveled as a coupleWritten August 6, 2025BrianMnjSparta, New Jersey1 contribution5 of 5 bubblesGreat place to visitHad a great time in historic New Castle! Didn’t know how old and historic the area is, learn a great deal about the history of the area. Had a great meal at Jessop's Tavern. Will be returning in the future.Review of: New Castle Visitor Center at The ArsenalVisited August 2025Traveled with familyWritten September 4, 20255 of 5 bubblesThe Incredible Liberty Encounters History TourOur family took the Liberty Encounters Tour on a late summer morning, and it was an incredible experience! The tour began along the Delaware River, where the breeze off the water, the flying colonial flag, and the authentic costumes of Mr. Bradford and his crew created a patriotic atmosphere that instantly transported us back hundreds of years. This was not an ordinary tour. Mr. Bradford’s passion for sharing our country’s history and heritage made every moment engaging. What impressed me most was how he invited us to act out real historical stories, which made history vivid. With the beat of a drum and the sound of melodious flute and patriotic songs, we marched through the beautiful old town of New Castle, visiting several historic sites along the way. It was fun, immersive, and educational — perfect for the whole family. I highly recommend this tour to students, visitors, history lovers, and even local Delawareans like myself. You’ll come away with a deeper appreciation of New Castle and our nation’s history. From my 13-year-old son’s perspective: “I recently joined this tour in New Castle, and it was amazing. The guide,Mr. Bradford, brought history to life through great storytelling and fun interactive activities. My favorite part was the musket demonstration and mini battle reenactment — watching the musket being loaded and fired with smoke, and participating in a skirmish made me feel like I was right there in the 1600s. The mix of fun and history was perfect. I definitely recommend this tour!”Dear Mrs. Yang, Thank you for such a marvelous review! 'Twas a joy to read what you and your family (including your eloquent son) thought about the History Adventure Tour. Thank you for the wonderful memories and time of fun learning together! We hope to march with you again sometime. Huzza for Liberty and Independence! Gratefully yours, Aaron BradfordWritten August 19, 2025This response is the subjective opinion of the management representative and not of Tripadvisor LLC.Review of: Liberty EncountersVisited August 2025Traveled with familyWritten August 18, 20255 of 5 bubblesSo Glad We Stopped HereOur first stop was to the visitors center to get some Information on local houses. Saved us time from going to 2 that were not open, although online information was as different. She gave us 3 different walking maps, one went with an auto tour. Very informative and helped us make the most of our time in New Castle.Review of: New Castle Visitor Center at The ArsenalVisited August 2025Traveled as a coupleWritten August 10, 20255 of 5 bubblesVery cool!What a neat place! We were lucky enough to arrive just as a tour was beginning & were welcomed in. Our tour guide breathed life into this interesting place by telling real stories about the people & events of Delaware's history. We learned a great deal & really enjoyed seeing the exhibits & other tangible mementos of our shared American history. Very dang cool.Review of: New Castle Court HouseVisited August 2025Traveled as a coupleWritten September 1, 20251 of 5 bubblesDo NOT fly Avelo, you’ll pay moreHorrible! I was charged $65 for a pocketbook at the gate (see picture), when I’ve traveled with the same bag and never been charged. Flights often get cancelled without warning. Paying extra for refundable flights does not get you a refund, but a voucher to fly with them again. If you have an issue, the average wait time for getting someone on the phone is 6-8 hours and the staff isn’t trained to help anyway. After you add the fees they tack on for no reason and are hidden charges, it’s cheaper to fly other airlines. Dirty, small planes but I guess that’s what happens when they are going out of business.Review of: Avelo AirlinesVisited March 2026Traveled with familyWritten March 18, 20265 of 5 bubblesHistory, Family, Faith, and Fun! Huzzah!We had a wonderful morning with Liberty Encounters. You can tell their family has a real passion for this. The pacing of the tour was excellent. The colonial games were so fun! They did an excellent job keeping the children engaged by providing multiple opportunities and ways to participate. Boys and girls seemed to enjoy the experience equally. I especially loved when we sang together in the meeting house. Other people could tell we were having fun too. Passersby kept coming up and asking what we were doing. Highly reccomend Liberty Encounters. Huzzah!Review of: Liberty EncountersVisited September 2025Traveled with familyWritten October 6, 20252 of 5 bubblesBad customer service. Bad carry on policyWe recently had a bad experience with Avelo employees. We traveled from the Tweed Airport in New Haven to Orlando. An employee at the Tweed airport was extremely rude. He had an argument with another passenger about priority seating. Rather than de-escalating the scenario he decided to berate the customer and accuse him of not listening over the gate 2 loud speaker. This employee was clearly frustrated and needed to step away from the situation. For our return flight from Orlando to Connecticut we dealt with an over aggressive employee regarding our personal/carry on items. I flew from Connecticut to Orlando with no carry on issues. I returned with the same items . My backpack was the same size as I did not bring anything extra back. This employee insisted that I pay $65 for my backpack. When I protested I was told that I “didn’t have to fly today”. Avelo’s carry on policy is completely subjective and apparently is decided upon by the employee at the gate. This woman was over the top aggressive and Avelo basically bullied me into paying an extra $65 in order to get on my return flight. My Avelo experience didn’t not meet expectations due to poor customer service.Review of: Avelo AirlinesVisited March 2026Traveled with familyWritten March 22, 2026These reviews are the subjective opinion of Tripadvisor members and not of Tripadvisor LLC.
